clue.text: Vain rules, unexpectedly widespread

indicators.note: something happening unexpectedly comes out differently, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pointless regulations have, surprisingly, spread everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Something universal applies everywhere and to everyone, the synonym sense of being broadly prevalent.

clue.text: One employing American English regularly at first

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word regularly

parts.note: its first letter is R

explanation.surface: Someone who habitually speaks American English.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is a person who makes use of something, so a synonym for someone putting a thing to work.

clue.text: Composer after frozen confection, an unemotional type

indicators.note: after means the composer's name comes behind the frozen treat in the answer

parts.note: ice, as in an ice lolly or water ice
Alban Berg, the Austrian composer

explanation.surface: A musician following an ice cream is a cold fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone an iceberg is an idiom for a person who shows no warmth or feeling.

clue.text: Greek character's estimated time of arrival

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet
second meaning: the common abbreviation for when something is due

explanation.surface: A Greek letter turns out to stand for an arrival estimate.
explanation.definitionFit: The same three letters name a letter of the Greek alphabet and abbreviate the expected arrival time.

clue.text: Heavenly body giving half of us a shock

indicators.note: half of the two-letter word us is a single letter, here its second

parts.note: its second half is S
a turn is a sudden fright, as in 'it gave me quite a turn'

explanation.surface: A celestial sight gives half of us a fright.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturn is a planet, an example of a celestial body in the night sky.

clue.text: Eg publicans disturbing silence outside quarters

indicators.note: outside means the rearranged letters go around the quarters
disturbing the word silence throws its letters into a new order

parts.note: the compass points south and east are quarters of the compass, S and E

explanation.surface: Pub landlords breaking the peace around their living quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a publican must hold a licence to sell alcohol, which is why publicans are the example here.
explanation.definitionFit: Publicans hold a licence to sell drink, so they are an example of licence holders.

clue.text: Chartered accountant imbibing hot drink

indicators.note: imbibing means taking in, so the accountant's letters hold the letter for hot

parts.note: CA is the abbreviation for chartered accountant; the answer's letters at the start of Chartered are a coincidence, not a hidden word
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: An accountant sipping a warm beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: Cha is British informal slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Cha is an informal word for tea, the classic British beverage.

clue.text: Soldier supporting head of cat or dog

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means the soldier's letters sit beneath the others
head of means the first letter of the word cat

parts.note: its first letter is C
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier holding up a cat or dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A corgi is a breed of short-legged Welsh dog, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Everyone, say, runs over, initially moving quickly

parts.note: everyone means all
say introduces an example, abbreviated EG

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the two words runs and over

parts.note: its first letter is R
its first letter is O

explanation.surface: Everybody runs over, starting off at speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegro is the musical direction for a brisk, lively tempo.

clue.text: Stylish English member meeting worker

parts.note: a limb is a member, here a leg
the worker ant is a crossword staple for worker

explanation.surface: A fashionable English politician meets a labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant describes someone graceful and refined in appearance, a synonym for being smart.

clue.text: Girl taking vehicle to school at last

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: at last takes the final letter of each of the words to and school

parts.note: its last letter is O
its last letter is L

explanation.surface: A girl getting a lift in the car to school, finally.
explanation.definitionFit: Carol is a female given name, so an example of a girl's name.

clue.text: Listen, being widely discussed on social media is agonising!

parts.note: to hear is to listen

parts.words: being widely discussed on social media
parts.note: a topic is trending when it is much talked about online

explanation.surface: An exclamation that what is going viral online is painful to hear.
explanation.definitionFit: Something heartrending causes great sorrow or distress, a synonym for painful.

clue.text: Wide boy always holding up item of tennis gear

indicators.note: in a down clue, holding up means the word for always sits below the tennis gear

parts.note: a racket is what a tennis player hits with
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A lad forever propping up his tennis racket.
explanation.walkthrough: A wide boy is British slang for a man who lives by shady dealing.
explanation.definitionFit: A racketeer runs a dishonest scheme, just as a wide boy is a petty swindler.

clue.text: Something left, for example, in flimsy wrapping?

indicators.note: in means the example abbreviation is placed inside the word for flimsy

parts.note: lacy fabric is delicate and flimsy

explanation.surface: A gift left behind, perhaps, in thin wrapping paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A legacy is something bequeathed in a will, what a person leaves behind.

clue.text: False reports about cat in French city

indicators.note: about means the false reports go around the cat

parts.note: lies are false statements
mog is British informal slang for a cat

explanation.surface: Untrue rumours concerning a cat in a city in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Limoges is a city in west-central France, famous for its porcelain.

clue.text: Male former partner in charge of old country

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner

explanation.surface: A man's former partner running an ancient land.
explanation.definitionFit: Mexico is a nation in North America, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Prize money wife has left for a spell of cricket

indicators.note: has left means the letter for wife departs from the prize money

parts.note: winnings are money won as a prize

explanation.surface: The wife has run off with the prize money, during a cricket session.
explanation.definitionFit: An innings is the period in cricket during which a batsman or team bats.

clue.text: Swirling mist restricts Rugby: an obvious fact

indicators.note: restricts means the swirled letters confine the rugby abbreviation inside them
swirling stirs the letters of mist about into a new order

parts.note: RU is the abbreviation for Rugby Union

explanation.surface: Fog closes in on a rugby match, which is plainly true.
explanation.definitionFit: A truism is a statement so self-evident it hardly needs saying.

clue.text: Distort terms in peer's broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: A lord twisting the conditions of a radio or TV transmission.
explanation.definitionFit: To misrepresent is to give a false account of something, twisting its true meaning.

clue.text: Cheery lad, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word for lad is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: sonny is a familiar way to address a boy

explanation.surface: A cheerful boy, so they say.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunny disposition is a bright, cheerful one.

clue.text: Headgear seen on European promontory

indicators.note: in a down clue, seen on means the headgear sits above the letter for European

parts.note: a cap is a hat

explanation.surface: A hat spotted on a European headland.
explanation.definitionFit: A cape is a headland jutting into the sea, a synonym for promontory.

clue.text: Information regarding a category of art

parts.note: gen is British informal for information
re means concerning or regarding

explanation.surface: Details about a type of artwork.
explanation.definitionFit: A genre is a style or kind of artistic work, such as a landscape or a thriller.

clue.text: Popular supporter cheers Spanish princess

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a fan is a supporter
ta is British informal for thanks, as is cheers

explanation.surface: A well-liked fan thanks a royal from Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Infanta is the title of a daughter of the Spanish or Portuguese monarch.

clue.text: Following peacekeepers is amusing

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
the UN sends peacekeeping forces

explanation.surface: Tracking the peacekeepers is entertaining.
explanation.definitionFit: Fun used as an adjective means enjoyable or entertaining.

clue.text: Animal pen in West Yorkshire

indicators.note: in means the letters lie within the run of the words West Yorkshire

explanation.surface: An enclosure for livestock in a northern English county.
explanation.definitionFit: A sty is an enclosure where pigs are kept.

clue.text: Conjure up memories about short skirts at church

parts.note: re means about or concerning
minis are miniskirts
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Recalling the days of miniskirts worn to church.
explanation.definitionFit: To reminisce is to recall and talk about past experiences with pleasure.
